headline: DonorPerfect restores its Classic Forms admin area; GoFundMe's Salesforce link still off; CanadaHelps outage noted, not tied.
summary: Update: DonorPerfect's status page (Nov 25, 8:11 AM ET) says the Classic Forms admin area and Review and Acceptance Center are restored; Classic Crowdfunding forms remain unavailable (c008, q005, new s014, t017). GoFundMe's status page (Nov 24, 5:37 PM ET) says the Salesforce integration remains disabled (c006, s002, t016). DonorPerfect's customer message, updated Nov 24, says it has not determined whether any organization's data was accessed (c009 stays Not established). The NonProfit Times (Nov 24, s012) reports the FBI was among agencies notified and declined to comment, and reports CanadaHelps disabled its donor management system while investigating an IT issue; no source ties that to these breaches (new c016, Not established). Third Sector (Nov 24, s013) relays GoFundMe's notice and says no UK charities had GoFundMe Pro accounts (c001). No label change on existing claims. Salesforce advisory unchanged (last updated Nov 20); DonorPerfect API and mobile app still unavailable (last update Nov 23). Still Not established: counts, DonorPerfect data impact, root cause, attacker, same attacker, tie to other outages. Carries forward u003 and u004 (not yet merged). No leak site, dark-web page or tracker visited. Privacy check done: no names of individuals, officials, reporters or spokespeople, no handles, contact details or phone numbers.

headline: DonorPerfect's Nov 23 status update: a fifth partner integration is rebuilt, but none is active yet.

headline: Salesforce's own public advisory found: it disabled the GoFundMe Pro connection over suspicious token use, not a Salesforce flaw.
summary: Label change: c007 (Salesforce says it disabled the GoFundMe Pro connected app over suspicious use of access tokens, and that this was not a flaw in Salesforce) moved from Reported to Confirmed. We found Salesforce's own Trust status advisory (s010, Tier 1), posted Nov 11 and updated Nov 20: Salesforce re-enabled the GoFundMe Pro managed packages on Nov 20, but the connected apps stay disabled until GoFundMe completes remediation; Salesforce says it will notify customers if it finds unauthorized access to their data. Confirmed covers what Salesforce says it did; that it was not a Salesforce flaw remains Salesforce's own account (q008 stays Reported). Added DonorPerfect's undated customer message (s011, Tier 1), which says it confirmed unauthorized activity involving certain systems and will send confirmed findings to affected organizations (c002, c009 detail). Timeline t012, t013. Status pages re-read: GoFundMe and DonorPerfect unchanged since Nov 20 and Nov 21 9:31 AM ET. Still Not established: counts, DonorPerfect data impact, root cause, attacker, same attacker, tie to other outages. A Tier 3 recap (The Nonprofit Herald) restates the same sources and was not added. No leak site, dark-web page or tracker visited. Privacy check done: no names of individuals, officials, reporters or spokespeople, no handles, contact details or phone numbers.

headline: Both companies confirm unauthorized access; who did it, how, and whether it was one attacker: not established.
summary: First draft. 9 sources (5 Tier 1, 3 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 15 claims (5 Confirmed, 5 Reported, 1 Unverified, 4 Not established), 10 questions. GoFundMe and DonorPerfect each admit unauthorized access on their own status pages (Confirmed). The AI bots and marketing website account, the Salesforce statement, the Salesforce credentials and the notification details are Reported from press quoting the companies. A claim that funds were diverted is Unverified. Counts, DonorPerfect data impact, attacker, same-attacker and any tie to the November outage wave are Not established. We did not visit any leak site, dark-web page or tracker. Corrections to the brief: DonorPerfect has not been offline continuously since Nov 10, it began staged restoration Nov 14 and only the API and mobile app remain down; GoFundMe public notice says donor credentials were not accessed, and card numbers and bank details were not accessed. Privacy check done: no names of individuals, officials, reporters or spokespeople, no handles, contact details or phone numbers.
